correctness.rationale: For crown graph K_{n,n} minus matching (n≥3), same-shore vertices have distance2 and their geodesic intervals cover opposite-shore indices other than the endpoint indices; an opposite-shore matched pair a_i,b_i has distance3 and varying intermediate paths covers the whole graph. Unmatched cross-shore pairs are adjacent and introduce no interior points. Thus any matched pair suffices; with X∩Y=∅, geodetic coverage occurs only for an entire shore or for both nonempty shores with |X|,|Y|≥3. These cases are disjoint and yield G_n(z)=(1+z)^(2n)−(1+2z)^n+2z^n+Σ_{k=6}^n C(n,k)(2^k−2−2k−k(k−1))z^k. Inclusion minimality forces exactly one matched pair, exactly an entire shore, or exactly 3 indices in each of two disjoint shores, yielding M_n(z)=n z²+2 z^n+C(n,3)C(n−3,3)z^6. All minimal sizes for n≥7 are {2,6,n}; upper geodetic n. Direct independent BFS distance-and-geodesic interval enumeration for n=3..5 agrees with classification and cardinality counts; the all-n proof is by exact intervals, not finite extrapolation.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are canonical regular vertex-transitive bipartite graphs obtained by deleting a perfect matching; geodetic coverage is a well-studied graph invariant. Their complete all-set and inclusion-minimal enumerators reveal a three-point minimal-cardinality spectrum and arbitrarily long gaps despite strong symmetry, a structural classification rather than an arbitrary sampled exact coefficient.

limitations: n≥3 connected crown graphs; ordinary all-shortest-path geodetic coverage not strong/hull geodetic; full older literature inaccessible and possible exact preexisting crown table unexcluded.
